topic: The mixed-state KD-real SLD exclusion conjecture after (6.23) in arXiv:2511.01996v2, Section 6.3
title: A KD-positive counterexample to the SLD conjecture in arXiv:2511.01996v2, Section 6.3 after (6.23), p. 43

creators.name: Wenlin Zhang
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We refute the mixed-state conjecture of Spriet, Langrenez, Brummelhuis and De Bièvre in arXiv:2511.01996v2, Section 6.3 immediately after (6.23), p. 43: a KD-real state and generator can have a KD-real symmetric logarithmic derivative with nonzero quantum Fisher information. Two rank-three projections in dimension nine give a faithful KD-positive state with quantum Fisher information 1/6. The construction gives a one-parameter family, two singular mixed endpoints, and counterexamples in every square dimension n^2 with n>=3. Exclusion holds for states in the real span of the two basis-diagonal spaces, for cyclic-prime Fourier bases, and for all KD-real states when the transition matrix is real up to basis phases. Exclusion also holds for Haar-almost every pair of bases in each finite dimension.
summary: Complete written proofs give square-dimensional counterexamples, endpoint states, SLD-optimal measurements, mixed-state exclusion conditions, including Haar-almost every pair of bases, and a star-algebra mechanism. The least counterexample dimension lies between three and nine. The pinned Lean result covers the concrete dimension-nine lambda=1 refutation. Exact arithmetic checks six rational parameters, two endpoints and square orders 2, 4 and 6. The coverage table separates these statements from cited pure-state and Fourier results and from questions not covered.
